bullets.title: The Handmaiden
bullets.note: I absolutely loved this movie. It’s beautiful, hilarious, horrifying, and sensual in equal measure. This BAFTA-winning film was introduced to me by recent podcast guest [Steve Jang](https://tim.blog/2023/11/30/steve-jang-live-from-south-korea/?utm_source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf#content) (see [his top-10 recommended Korean films here](https://tim.blog/2023/11/30/steve-jang-live-from-south-korea/?utm_source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf#content)), and it currently has 96% on [Rotten Tomatoes](https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/the_handmaiden). Description: “From Park Chan-wook, the celebrated director of _Oldboy_, _Lady Vengeance_ and _Stoker_, comes a ravishing new crime drama. Park presents a gripping and sensual tale of two women—a young Japanese lady living on a secluded estate and a Korean woman who is hired to serve as her new handmaiden but is secretly plotting with a conman to defraud her of a large inheritance. Inspired by the novel _Fingersmith_ by British author Sarah Waters, _The Handmaiden_ borrows the most dynamic elements of its source material and combines it with Park Chan-wook’s singular vision to create an unforgettable viewing experience.” You can find the trailer [here](https://youtu.be/whldChqCsYk?feature=shared).

bullets.title: The Greatest Submission Artist – Gordon Ryan
Lululemon’s Founder Is Racing to Cure the Rare Disease Destroying His Muscles
bullets.creator: Ari Altstedter
bullets.note:
(_Bloomberg_). [Alternate article link](https://archive.ph/8z9Af), in case you have any issues accessing using the previous one.  
​  
From the sub-heading: “For decades, Chip Wilson has been facing a form of muscular dystrophy. Now the notoriously unfiltered billionaire is spending $100 million to cure it.”

Sometimes, the ultra-rich can produce breakthroughs in medicine, if they’re willing to spend big and take risks. Chip is willing to do both. Survival is one hell of a motivator. Here’s one excerpt from the piece:  
​  
​_“If you’re going to be in a foxhole, being in one with Chip Wilson feels a little less suffocating,” says Craig Kelley, a 53-year-old FSHD patient. Kelley, who has difficulty going up stairs and can’t take off a T-shirt without bracing himself, guesses the odds of a cure have “tripled” since Wilson got involved. “I hope anybody with any kind of long-term disability can have a bit of a game changer like Chip.”  
​  
​_There are also some incredible examples of non-rich people doing the seemingly impossible to save family members. I strongly recommend listening to “[John Crowley — The Real-Life Captain America and Bruce Banner (Seriously)](https://tim.blog/2017/02/28/john-crowley/?utm_source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf#content),” whose story has been the basis of both books and feature films.
